chunks: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorified, did not grant Satan authority over those who believe and are pious; and when they do [act], [it is] those who believe, then become pious, then believe, then become pious. And Allah loves the pious.
Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorified, did not grant Satan authority over those who believe and are pious.
And when they do [act], [it is] those who believe, then become pious, then believe, then become pious. And Allah loves the pious.
He said: This is in reference to His Exalted and Glorified saying: 'His authority is only over those who take him as a guardian and those who associate him with Allah.'

key_terms.الْمُتَّقِينَ: The pious, those who practice taqwa
key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُ: They take him as a guardian/ally

ai.seo_question: What is the extent of Satan's authority over believers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying that Satan's authority is not absolute but conditional upon the believer's choice, specifically linking it to the concept of *khuwwan* (taking Satan as a close ally). This distinction underscores the Shia theological principle that while all humans are susceptible to whispering, true piety acts as a shield, limiting Satan's influence to those who actively align with his guidance rather than those merely exposed to it.
